title: THC Apple Cider: Mulled Cannabis Hot Cider Recipe
h1: Warm Spiced Apple Cider with a Measured Infusion
metaDescription: Mull THC apple cider with whole spices, then stir in a measured tincture, glycerin tincture or canna-honey, with per-mug dosing and a slow-cooker party plan.
excerpt: A spiced fall mug that simmers plain, takes a measured infusion at the end and comes with a slow-cooker setup that keeps every guest's dose clear.
keyTakeaways: Simmer the spices in plain cider; add the infusion last, on the lowest heat.
Divide the total THC by the number of mugs and stir well so each mug matches.
For parties, keep plain cider in the slow cooker and dose individual, marked mugs.
Infused cider can be slow to kick in, so finish one mug and wait before another.
body:
THC apple cider turns a cozy fall and winter mug into an adults-only sip with a dose you can count. Spices simmer in plain cider, and the infusion goes in last, on the lowest heat.

## Dosing THC Apple Cider Safely

Divide your total THC by the number of mugs (the recipe card shows the math), and when hosting, dose individual mugs, never the pot.

Mulled cider with THC is meant for adults 21 and older. Like other edibles, it can be slow to register, sometimes up to 2 hours. Finish one mug, then give it the full 2 hours before deciding on another; our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/) walks through choosing a first amount.

## What Goes In

Use unfiltered cider, whole cinnamon, star anise and cloves (they strain out cleanly), a little ginger and your sweetener of choice; orange simmers in and apple slices garnish. Dose with an alcohol or glycerin tincture ([tincture basics](/blog/cannabis-tincture-guide/)) or [canna-honey](/blog/canna-honey/); oil-based drops tend to float on cider rather than mix in. Prefer a labeled product? Browse [High Society's online menu](/shop/) (each store's selection differs) and order ahead for pickup.

## How to Mull It

Steep the spices and half the orange in cider just below a simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, then strain and sweeten. Drop the burner to its lowest setting before stirring in the infusion: it only needs warming, and long, hot cooking can cost some THC. Ladle with a measuring cup so the mugs match.

## Storage and Labeling

Refrigerate leftovers in a jar marked "THC," dated and showing the dose per cup, and finish them within a few days. Warm single cups gently; there's no need to boil.

## Party Version: A Labeled Dosing Station

For a holiday crowd, keep plain cider on the slow cooker's warm setting so everyone can help themselves. Beside it, set up a dosing station for guests 21 and older who want an infused mug. Lay out the infusion, an oral syringe or measuring spoons, a card listing the dose per milliliter or teaspoon, and marked mugs for infused servings. Stay with the station, keep the infusion out of reach of kids and pets, and pack it all away afterward. For another seasonal sip, see our [fruitcake canna-cocktail](/blog/fruitcake-canna-cocktail/).

faq.q: Does heating cider destroy the THC?
faq.a: Not at gentle heat. Infusions made from decarboxylated cannabis already hold active THC, so they only need warming. Lab work on cannabis extracts has measured THC losses when heat runs high for a long time, so add the infusion last and keep the pot below a simmer.

faq.q: Can canna-honey be the sweetener and the dose?
faq.a: Yes, but measure it for the dose, not for taste. Sweeten the cider with plain honey or maple syrup first, then stir in the measured canna-honey. If a mug still tastes flat, add plain honey, never more of the infused kind.

A cannabis tincture made with food-grade vegetable glycerin instead of alcohol. It tastes sweet, has no alcohol bite and mixes easily into warm drinks. Its strength depends on how it was made, so dose it from the label or your batch notes, and expect edible timing once it's in the cider.

ingredients: 4 cups (1 quart) apple cider, unfiltered if you can find it
1 to 2 tablespoons maple syrup, honey or brown sugar, to taste
A measured infusion for 4 servings: alcohol tincture, glycerin tincture or canna-honey (see the dosing note)
steps: Combine the cider, cinnamon, star anise, cloves, ginger and half the orange rounds in a saucepan. Bring just to a simmer over medium heat.
Lower the heat and let the spices steep for 15 to 20 minutes without boiling.
Strain out the spices and orange. Taste, then sweeten with plain maple syrup, honey or sugar.
Turn the burner to its lowest setting. Add the measured infusion and stir for 30 seconds, until any canna-honey has fully dissolved.
Divide evenly among 4 mugs with a measuring cup. Garnish with apple slices and the remaining orange rounds, and mark the infused mugs if plain cider is also being served.
recipe.dosingNote: **THC per mug = total THC added ÷ 4.** With a tincture labeled 10 mg per ml, 1 ml in the pot adds about 10 mg, or about 2.5 mg per mug. With canna-honey estimated at 10 mg per teaspoon, 1 teaspoon does the same. Count both as estimates. Michigan labels carry a note that the real THC content can vary by 10%, and a homemade infusion's strength hinges on the flower you used and on what decarboxylation and infusion take away. Start low with one mug, wait at least 2 hours before another, and keep leftovers labeled and away from kids and pets.

sources.label: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention: Cannabis frequently asked questions
Wang M. et al. (2016), Decarboxylation study of acidic cannabinoids, Cannabis and Cannabinoid Research
Michigan Cannabis Regulatory Agency: Marihuana Rules, R 420.1 to R 420.1004 (product labeling, PDF)

review.summary: 14 claims checked: 12 ok, 2 fixed (1 wrong, 0 unsupported, 1 overstated); 3 ok claims also got safety or wording edits.

claims.claim: Mulled cider with THC is meant for adults 21 and older
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-au-age (MRTMA: legal for adults 21+, does not cover anyone under 21)

claims.claim: Like other edibles, infused cider can be slow to register, sometimes up to 2 hours (body, takeaway)
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html (WebFetch 2026-10-24): "since it can take up to 2 hours to feel the effects from the drug"; "Eating or drinking foods with cannabis can take longer to have an effect"

claims.claim: Finish one mug before deciding on another
claims.fix: safety wording: now "Finish one mug, then give it the full 2 hours before deciding on another", matching the takeaway and the dosing note's 2-hour wait
claims.source: CDC cannabis FAQ (above): up to 2 hours to feel effects

claims.claim: Infusions made from decarboxylated cannabis already hold active THC, so they only need warming (FAQ, body)
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ (Wang et al. 2016, PMID 28861498; abstract and full text read via Europe PMC): heating converts the acidic cannabinoids (THCA-A) in C. sativa extracts into neutral THC

claims.claim: Long cooking can degrade THC; lab work on cannabis extracts has measured THC losses when heat runs high for a long time; gentle heat does not destroy it (body, FAQ)
claims.fix: the evidence shows losses with long, high heat, not with long cooking as such (the site's own cannabutter recipe holds infusions at a bare simmer for 3 to 4 hours); body now "long, hot cooking can cost some THC"; the FAQ ("Not at gentle heat"; losses "when heat runs high for a long time") already matched the evidence
claims.source: Wang et al. 2016 full text (Europe PMC): describing Veress et al., "Maximum formation of Δ9-THC was observed in ∼5–10 min at 145°C followed by a significant loss at longer times possibly due to evaporation of Δ9-THC"; Wang's own extracts, heated at 80-145°C for up to 60 min in a vacuum oven: "The sum of the molar concentration of THCA-A and Δ9-THC decreased slightly"; oxygen and light "could possibly produce decomposition of Δ9-THC to CBN". The writer's quote is Wang's summary of the earlier study, not Wang's own result.

claims.claim: Stir the infusion for 30 seconds until no streaks of honey or oil remain (recipe step 4)
claims.fix: oil does not dissolve in cider, so oil streaks never stir away; the step now reads "until any canna-honey has fully dissolved", and What Goes In now ends its dosing sentence with "oil-based drops tend to float on cider rather than mix in" (the menu link could lead readers to oil-based drops)
claims.source: general chemistry: oils are immiscible with water and less dense, so they float; glycerin and ethanol are water-miscible

claims.claim: A glycerin tincture is made with food-grade vegetable glycerin instead of alcohol, tastes sweet, has no alcohol bite, mixes easily into warm drinks, and its strength depends on how it was made (FAQ)
claims.source: general knowledge (glycerol is sweet-tasting and water-miscible); no health claim

claims.claim: Once a tincture is in the cider, expect edible timing (FAQ)
claims.source: CDC cannabis FAQ (above): eating or drinking cannabis "can take longer to have an effect"

claims.claim: Michigan labels carry a note that the real THC content can vary by 10% (dosing note)
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-labeling details (R 420.504(1)); wording confirmed on the Cornell LII copy of R 420.504(1)(f) (WebFetch 2026-10-24), since michigan.gov refuses automated fetches: "along with a statement that the actual value may vary from the reported value by 10%"; the CRA rules PDF already cited is the law-facts source

claims.claim: Dose math: total THC ÷ 4 mugs; a 10 mg/ml tincture, 1 ml in the pot, is about 10 mg or 2.5 mg per mug; canna-honey at an estimated 10 mg per teaspoon does the same; both are estimates
claims.fix: none (arithmetic checked: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5; figures are labeled examples, not facts about any product)
claims.source: arithmetic; build contract section 4 recipe rule

claims.claim: A homemade infusion's strength hinges on the starting flower and on what decarboxylation and infusion take away (dosing note)
claims.fix: wording: "Start with one mug" became "Start low with one mug" so the note says to start low and wait
claims.source: Wang et al. 2016 (above): decarboxylation converts THCA to THC with some loss; task recipe rule

claims.claim: Browse High Society's online menu (each store's selection differs) and order ahead for pickup
claims.fix: none (no product named or said to be stocked)
claims.source: facts/hs-facts.json services.ordering ("Online order for pickup"), services.productCategories (tinctures appear on some store menus); docs/structure-map.json: /shop/ is the store-menu chooser

claims.claim: Refrigerate labeled leftovers and finish them within a few days; reheat gently without boiling
claims.source: general food-safety practice (a conservative window for opened cider)

claims.claim: Party version: plain cider self-serve in the slow cooker, with the infusion, a syringe or spoons, a dose card and marked mugs set out beside it; stay nearby
claims.fix: safety wording: the station is now for guests 21 and older who want an infused mug, the host stays with it, and the infusion is kept out of reach of kids and pets (a holiday crowd can include children)
claims.source: brief mustAvoid (no serving to anyone under 21, nothing within reach of kids or pets); facts/law-facts.json mi-au-age

review.notes: Independent fact-check: the CDC FAQ was reopened with WebFetch; Wang et al. 2016 was read through Europe PMC (abstract and full text); the R 420.504(1)(f) label wording was confirmed on the Cornell LII copy because michigan.gov refuses fetches, and the CRA PDF from law-facts stays the cited source. High Society facts used: online ordering for pickup and the /shop/ menu chooser only; no product said to be stocked, and no phone, hours, address, payment, prices, deals or app. Writer's notes: Liquor never suggested; plain pot plus dosed mugs for gatherings; dose figures are labeled examples. No store phone, hours, address, payment, prices or product stock claims.
